user.title: SG Smart Gen1 (CSRmesh)
user.description: Enter the network passphrase of your SG installation (usually 1234). A raw 16-byte network key in hex overrides the passphrase.

error.invalid_key: The key must be 32 hex characters.

abort.already_configured: The SG Gen1 network is already set up.

init.title: SG Smart Gen1
init.description: What do you want to do?

menu_options.migrate_device: Move a device from the SG gateway

remove_device.title: Remove a device
remove_device.description: With factory reset the device also leaves the mesh (as when deleting it in the SG app), so it can be added again with Add a new device. Without it, the device is only removed from HA and keeps working in the mesh; a device moved from the SG gateway goes back to the gateway's HomeKit entities.

data_description.poll_interval: The dimmers do not report changes by themselves; HA asks for status this often.
data_description.min_level: Lowest level HA sends, to keep the slider out of the dimmer's dead zone.

add_by_address.title: Add by mesh address
add_by_address.description: Pick a mesh address heard on the network (run "Capture frames" first and toggle the lamp), or type the address in hex, e.g. CA67.

migrate_device.title: Move from SG gateway
migrate_device.description: {count} devices are still owned by the SG gateway (through HomeKit). Pick one. HA will make the gateway talk to it and watch the mesh to find its address: a lamp switches briefly on or off, a thermostat's set-point moves half a degree for a moment, and for a Smart Switch you press a button.

data.hide_homekit: Disable the gateway's HomeKit copy afterwards

migrate_press.title: Press a button on {name}
migrate_press.description: Click Submit, then press any button on **{name}** within a minute. The switch's own message tells HA its address.

migrate_confirm.title: Found {name}
migrate_confirm.description: **{name}** ({model}) has mesh address **{address}**. Did the right device react? You can flash it once more from HA directly (without the gateway) to be sure.

add_new.title: Add a new device
add_new.description: Power the new device (a battery switch: press a button to wake it) and keep it close to an existing SG Gen1 device. HA joins it to your network with the network PIN; the SG gateway is not involved. Click Submit to search.

add_new_pick.title: Found {count} new device(s)
add_new_pick.description: Devices are listed by their Bluetooth address (printed on some labels).

add_new_none.title: No new devices found
add_new_none.description: Nothing answered. Is the device factory reset and powered, and a battery switch awake? Some devices only accept joining for a few minutes after power-up.

remove_press.title: Wake {name}
remove_press.description: Click Submit, then press any button on {name} within a minute. HA sends the reset while it is awake.

progress.identify: Making the SG gateway talk to {name} and watching the mesh …
progress.switch: Waiting for a button press on {name} …
progress.associate: Joining {name} to the network (key exchange, up to a minute) …

abort.nothing_to_migrate: Every SG Gen1 device from the gateway has been moved.
abort.identify_no_reaction: {name} did not show up in the mesh. Is the gateway online, and does the device work from HomeKit? For a switch: press a button within the minute.
abort.identify_ambiguous: Several devices reacted at the same time. Try {name} again.
abort.identify_homekit_unavailable: The gateway's HomeKit entity for {name} is unavailable.
abort.identify_no_homekit_entity: {name} has no HomeKit light or thermostat to trigger.
abort.add_new_failed: Could not add {name}: {error}. Power-cycle the device and try again; after a failed attempt a device may refuse for about two minutes.
abort.reset_no_press: {name} did not wake up within a minute; nothing was changed.
abort.reset_still_in_mesh: {name} is still answering on the mesh, so it was not factory reset. It stays in Home Assistant; nothing was changed.

capture.name: Capture frames
capture.description: Log every decrypted frame on your network for a while. Use it to map Smart Switch and HeatReg messages.

send.name: Send raw mesh messages (developer)
send.description: Seal and send MCP messages given as hex (destination LE + opcode + body).

send_on_press.name: Send when a switch wakes (developer)
send_on_press.description: Wait for the next message from a battery switch, then send the messages while it is awake.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long to wait for a press.
